To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

GluN2A, GluN2C, and GluN2E subunits are present in NMDARs on dopaminergic neurons in the SNc of the mouse brain, that GluN1/GluN2D-containing NMDARs are present in both synaptic and extrasomatic locations, and that GluN3 subunits are not detectable in dopaminergic neurons.
the GluN subunit composition of NMDAR responses is altered in Grin2d null mice.

the GluN1/GluN2B NMDA receptor is the predominant synaptic receptor in substantia nigra pars compacta (SNc) dopaminergic (DA) neurons, and the GluN4B/GluN2D NMDA receptor predominates at extrasynaptic locations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of NMDAR subunits in the function of NMDAR-mediated synaptic and extrasynapic currents in SNc- DA neurons.
the role of NMDA receptor subunits in the function of the dopaminergic system.
understanding the mechanisms of synaptic plasticity and the role of NMDAR subtypes in the pathophysiology of neurological diseases such as epilepsy, schizophrenia and Parkinson’s disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

GluN2A and GluN2C subunits are present at both synaptic and extra-synaptic sites, while GluN2N and GluN3B are present extrasynaptically and that GluN3A is present extrasynapticaly and GluN1 is present at both locations in SNc DA neurons.
the GluN1/GluN2D NMDAR subunit combination is present at both synaptic and extra-synaptic locations in substantia nigra DA neurons.
the GluN1-GluN2D NMDAR is expressed in the brain.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
GluN2A and GluN2C-containing NMDARs are the major synaptic NMDARs, whereas GluN2AB-containing NMDAR is the major extrasynaptic NMRDAR in SNc- DA neurons.
the Grin2D subunit is important for the function of NMDAR in SNc- DA neurons.
the Grin2D subunit is present in both synaptic and extrasnaptic NMDA receptors in SNc- DA neurons, and the Grin2B subunit is present at synaptic NMDARs, but not extrasynaptic NMRARs in SN-DA neurons.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the GluN1/GluN2A-containing receptors in the brain are not as sensitive to DQP1105 as the GluN3A-containing receptors, and this difference may be important in the context of drug development.
GluN2A, GluN2C, and GluN2G subunits are expressed in SNc- DA neurons, and that the GluN1/GluN2A, and GluNI/GluN2C subunit combinations are the most abundant NMDARs expressed in SNc DA neurons.
GluN2A, GluN2C and GluN2E subunits can be substituted for GluN1/GluN2D NMDARs, but not GluN2F subunits.
